topics.description: The paramount leader of China during the 1989 Tiananmen protests and the government crackdown that followed.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The April 26 Editorial criticized people in this location, some of whom went on a hunger strike  prior to a Soviet leader's visit. People at this location drafted a list of seven demands that  denounced the campaign against “bourgeois (booj-wah) liberalization.” Jeff Widener (*) photographed a man in this location whom Time Magazine dubbed the “Unknown Rebel.” Taiwan,  Tibet, and this location form the “three Ts” of contentious issues surrounding the CCP. For 10 points,  name this public area in Beijing where the Tank Man photo was taken in 1989.

topics.description: Jacob Zuma is a South African politician who served as president from 2009 to 2018 and was later imprisoned for refusing to testify before the Zondo Commission.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 2018, this politician established the Zondo Commission to investigate corruption. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this former president who was sentenced to fifteen months in jail, ending in October 2022,  after refusing to testify before the commission.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Zuma was the fourth president of this country, whose first president under universal suffrage was  Nelson Mandela.
parts.answer: South Africa [Republic of South Africa; or RSA]

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 2021, a conflict regarding this industry near Cape Town resulted in the deaths of over 80 people.  The CPNC license, or “medallion,” needed to work in this industry has dropped in value in the U.S.  since the mid-2010s.

topics.description: A seventeenth-century Chinese military leader who expelled the Dutch from Taiwan and founded the Kingdom of Tungning.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This island’s indigenous Gaoshan people are descended from Austronesian settlers. On this island, the Kingdom of Tungning was established by the pirate Koxinga. Descendents of Hakka hill people make up about 20 percent of this island’s population. Fort Zeelandia was an early trading post on this island, whose colonial name comes from the (*) Portuguese for “beautiful island.” This island was held under martial law during the White Terror. After the Chinese Civil War, Chiang Kai-Shek and the rest of the Kuomintang fled to this island. For 10 points, Formosa was the former name of what island off the coast of southern China?
parts.answer: ANSWER: Taiwan [prompt on Formosa before mention]

topics.description: The Greek state and monarchy established after the Greek War of Independence, whose first king was Otto I of Greece.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer the following about imported German princes who were made rulers in the Balkans:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Otto I from the House of Wittelsbach was installed as the king of this country after it won its independence. This country’s war for independence saw Edward Codrington defeat the Ottoman navy at the Battle of Navarino.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] William of Wied, the new prince of Albania, quickly faced pressure from this empire to provide troops for World War I. The war was sparked by the assassination of this dual monarchy’s Archduke Franz Ferdinand by a Serb.
parts.answer: Austria-Hungary [or Austro-Hungarian Empire; prompt on Austria or Hungary]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A German prince with this name from the House of Battenberg was forced to abdicate as prince of Bulgaria just seven years after taking the throne. Troops of a different ruler with this name fought with Bulgarian volunteers against the Ottomans at the Battle of Shipka Pass.
parts.answer: Alexander [accept Alexander of Battenberg or Tsar Alexander II of Russia]

topics.description: An archaeological site in Suffolk famous for its richly furnished Anglo-Saxon ship burial and associated treasures.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This city contains a sculpture of a warrior queen in a chariot, named Boadicea and her Daughters near its legislative offices in Portcullis House. Four lion statues that were made from melted-down (*) French cannons stand in this city’s Trafalgar Square. The treasures of Sutton Hoo, an Anglo-Saxon ship burial, are held in a museum in, for ten points, what city, the home of Westminster Palace and Big Ben, that is the capital of England?

topics.description: The vast Eurasian empire ruled by the Romanov dynasty until the Russian Revolution of 1917.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This event occurred after a driver made a wrong turn to a street where, according to popular legend, its perpetrator had stopped to get a sandwich. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Describe this event was perpetrated by Gavrilo Princip in Sarajevo by a Serbian nationalist group.
parts.answer: assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand [accept any obvious equivalents, prompt on but DO NOT OTHERWISE REVEAL answers like the start of World War I]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Franz Ferdinand's death sparked the beginning of this war which lasted from 1914 to 1918.
parts.answer: World War I [or the First World War, or the Great War; accept The War to End All Wars]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This country was the first to mobilize forces to support Serbia, although it withdrew from the war after a 1917 revolution deposed its king Nicholas II.

topics.description: A Czech theologian and religious reformer whose preaching and writings anticipated aspects of the Protestant Reformation and led to his execution at the Council of Constance.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The number “135797531” (read the individual digits) was carved near a bridge in this city to  mark the moment when Charles IV (the fourth) began its construction. Ottokar I (oh-tah-KAR the  first) of the Přemyslid (PREM-iz-lid) dynasty reigned from this city, in whose outskirts Frederick V  (the fifth) the Winter King lost the throne at the Battle of (*) White Mountain. The theologian Jan  Hus (yahn hoos) spent much of his life in this city. The Thirty Years War began after officials were  thrown out windows in the second “defenestration of” this city. For 10 points, name this most populous  Bohemian and Czech city.

topics.description: A close-order infantry formation in which overlapping shields protect soldiers and create a unified wall of defense.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After this battle was won by an alliance of Athenian and Plataean [pla-TAY-un] warriors, news of the result was very quickly sent to Athens by a single runner, who legendarily dropped dead on arrival. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this 490 BCE battle that inspires the name of a modern, 26-mile-long footrace.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This is the Greek term for a spear-and-shield wielding footsoldier. Ten thousand of these soldiers from Athens joined another thousand from Plataea at Marathon.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hoplite soldiers became much more effective after they adopted this defensive formation, which was first used against a foreign enemy at Marathon. In this formation, hoplites are arrayed in long lines, with each using their shield to protect both themselves and the hoplite on their left.

topics.description: The Stasi was the secret police and intelligence service of East Germany, formally known as the Ministry for State Security.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s first Chancellor, Konrad Adenauer (AH-den-ow-er), presided over its economic miracle, which is also called Wirtschaftswunder (veer-CHAHFTS-voonder) or the Miracle on the Rhine. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this country which was part of the Western Bloc during the Cold War. Willy Brandt, a leader of this country, championed its philosophy of Ostpolitik which sought to normalize relations with its eastern neighbor.
parts.answer: West Germany [accept Federal Republic of Germany or FRG or BRD or Bonn Republic; prompt on Germany; do not accept or prompt on “East Germany” or “German Democratic Republic” or “GDR” or “DDR”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Willy Brandt’s government toppled when it was revealed that one of his advisors, Gunter Guillaume, was an agent for this organization. This organization was the secret police force of East Germany.
parts.answer: Stasi [accept Ministry for State Security or State Security Service]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Although this city was fully inside East Germany, it was separated into West and East portions by an eponymous wall. This city is the current capital of Germany.

topics.description: The deportation and exile of many Judeans to Babylon after Nebuchadnezzar II conquered Judah and destroyed the First Temple in Jerusalem.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this city, the Etemenanki Temple and the Ishtar Gate were constructed by King Nebuchadnezzar. After a ruler of this city destroyed Solomon's Temple, the Jews suffered a namesake (*) "captivity" in this city. Legal principles like "an eye for an eye" were established in this city by its ruler Hammurabi. For 10 points, name this Mesopotamian city home to some legendary Hanging Gardens.
